From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: calca, calcá, calçà, and călca

Catalan

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Early Medieval Latin calcea, from Latin calceus (“shoe”). Over time the meaning extended upward to include all of the body from the waist down, then contracted to cover only the area just below the waist.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈkal.sə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈkal.sa]

Noun

[edit]

calça f (plural calces)

  1. (archaic) sock
    Synonym: mitjó
  2. hose
    Synonym: mitja
  3. (in the plural) pantaloons; knickers
    Synonym: pantaló
  4. (in the plural) panties
    Synonym: calçó
  5. (agriculture) the outer bark of a cork oak that is put back on the tree after the cork has been harvested so as to help the tree to survive and produce more cork
Derived terms
[edit]
  • calça d'arena
  • calces de ferro
  • calceta
  • calceter
  • calçó
  • ésser un calces
Related terms
[edit]
  • calçar
  • calcar

Further reading

[edit]
  • “calça” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.
  • “calça”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026
  • “calça”, in Diccionari de la llengua catalana [Dictionary of the Catalan Language] (in Catalan), second edition, Institute of Catalan Studies [Catalan: Institut d'Estudis Catalans], April 2007

calça

Etymology 1

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
calça
Wikipedia pt

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese calça, from Early Medieval Latin calcea, from Latin calceus (“shoe”).

Noun

[edit]

calça f (plural calças)

  1. (chiefly in the plural) trousers, pants
  2. ring (on a mushroom)
Related terms
[edit]
  • calçar
  • calcar
  • coice
